reference_action: Give the drought-stressed plant a good drink; OP says they did so and it is fine.

sources.reason: At 0:42–1:02 lack of water is explained and adding water is the remedy; the two-week unattended sun exposure makes this branch applicable.

The readable caption only says check moisture and adjust frequency, without telling the owner to rehydrate; increasing light is also inappropriate to the stated sun exposure. Video content beyond the caption remains unverified.
At 0:52–1:21, increase watering when the plant is underwatered; this supplies the validated watering action.
Comments say to check that the center gets water and to water more, supplying the successful rehydration action.
Multiple comments recommend a big drink after sun-related drying; that is the OP-validated action, even though the source discusses peppers.

actions.action: Water if the wilt is caused by lack of water
Increase humidity around leaves for heat stress without wetting them
Check whether leaves regain rigidity in evening
Assess and manage under/overwatering if wilting persists
Flush soil if excess fertilizer salts caused wilting

resolved.reason: The first explanation supplies the correct watering fix, but several alternative causes remain and the diagnosis is not tailored to the two-week absence.

harmfulness.reason: “More water is not going to help” under anaerobic conditions warns against indiscriminate watering. The humidity discussion also avoids wetting leaves due to mildew risk; the salt-flushing instruction is less precise but does not create a likely case-specific harm here.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “Lack of water” and “simply add water” match the confirmed drought stress. The answer devotes comparable space to heat, overwatering, mechanical damage and salts instead of using the two-week absence to prioritize the cause.

feasibility.reason: Adding water and checking recovery in the evening are easy. “Assess or manage” under/overwatering and increasing humidity without wetting leaves leave parts of the procedure unspecified.
